We experienced a severe degradation across our checkout microservice yesterday (Nov 7) between 14:05–14:38 PST. Client-facing latencies spiked to 6–8s for LLM-powered completion calls and we observed a 12% 5xx error rate during the window. This materially affected conversion for a ~45-minute period.

We need a clear RCA, mitigation plan, and an executive readout. Specifically:
- Confirm root cause and affected capacity/regions
- Planned immediate fixes and timeline for deployment
- Compensation/credits approach for the incident window
- Ongoing monitoring/guardrails to prevent recurrence

Can your team deliver a preliminary RCA by EOD PT today and a 30-minute exec readout on Tue Nov 10? Our Head of Ops (Rajiv Patel) and sourcing team will join.

Sophie

Subject: Re: Major performance impact on peak window — technical RCA draft

Team —

Quick technical notes (draft):

Timeline & observables:
- 14:04:48 PST: sudden spike in concurrent inference requests from NorthForge (burst from scheduled batch + user-peaks).
- 14:05–14:13 PST: token-latency increase correlating with KV cache thrashing on our LRU eviction path.
- 14:13–14:38 PST: a subset of requests experienced serialization on CPU-GPU synchronization path; retry logic triggered and caused a 5xx spike (~12%).

Root cause (working):
1) Under extreme, short-lived concurrency bursts our prefix/KV cache eviction heuristics moved to a worst-case pattern — thrashing caused higher CPU overhead and longer serialization into GPU dispatch.
2) A regression in the scheduler's fast-path disabled a fallback queuing bucket for small, latency-sensitive requests when batch size exceeded threshold; this increased queuing delay.
3) Combined with a previously-unseen request pattern from the NorthForge batch job, it surfaced as increased latencies and errors.

Immediate corrective actions (next 72h):
- Push patch: reinstate conservative fallback queueing when per-model concurrency over threshold (hotfix to runtime) — target: Nov 9 02:00 PT canary, Nov 9 06:00 PT full deploy if green.
- Adjust KV cache parameters for the affected model class to reduce LRU churn under burst patterns — config change today, rollback-safe.
- Route NorthForge peak traffic to reserved capacity for 24 hours starting Nov 9 05:00 PT (manual route override).
- Add an alert for KV eviction rate and CPU-to-GPU dispatch latency; threshold set to 3x baseline.

Longer-term fixes (30d):
- Improve cache admission policy (work in Q4 roadmap).
- Scheduler rewrite for better fairness across latency-sensitive vs throughput batches.

Attachments: technical notes and traces attached. I will follow with a succinct exec summary to laura for the readout.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
